answer: Each epoch an agent buys one ripple per fable whose signature its epoch needs, and every ripple is priced by its place in that epoch's shared queue: the n-th ripple minted burns 2^(n−1)×base out of the buyer's vault. Wallet-splitting buys nothing, since the ladder counts mints, not wallets, so an operator fielding k clones pays base×(2^k −1) every epoch, its own heads pushing each other up the rungs. A newcomer buys the first ripple at base.
